subject: Hosted API unit pricing and model matrix
messages:
From: Cory Taylor <cory.taylor@acmeai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick question on hosted API unit pricing & model matrix

Hi Logan,

We're evaluating Redwood for a chat/assistant workflow and need a quick baseline for pricing and model availability. Could you send your standard per-1M token rates (input vs output) for the hosted API, plus a short model matrix — recommended models for conversational and summarization workloads and the relative cost tiers? We're estimating about 10M tokens/month to start, with intermittent spikes for demos and customer trials.

Also curious whether you have standard discount breakpoints for commit tiers (100M, 500M, etc.) and whether streaming vs non-streaming pricing differs. A simple table or a one-page PDF would be ideal.

Thanks — appreciate a quick pointer so we can budget this week.

Best,
Cory
Cory Taylor
Head of Platform, Acme AI
cory.taylor@acmeai.com
(415) 555-0112

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Cory Taylor <cory.taylor@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on hosted API unit pricing & model matrix

Hi Cory — thanks for the note and the context. Putting a concise baseline together below and attaching our one-page hosted rate summary. I can loop in engineering for latency numbers if you want model-by-model p50/p95.

Attachment: redwood-hosted-unit-pricing-20270312.pdf

Baseline (hosted API) — per 1M tokens (USD, input/output):
- Standard conversational models (r-instruct-small / r-chat-medium): input $0.45 / output $0.75
- Production conversational (r-chat-large): input $0.95 / output $1.40
- High-capacity LLMs (r-llm-xl / r-1-large): input $1.50 / output $2.50
- Embeddings (per 1k tokens equivalent): $0.20

Notes:
- Streaming token pricing follows the same input/output split; only billable tokens are counted.
- We publish a model matrix in the attached PDF with recommended use-cases and relative latencies.
- Standard discounts by committed monthly volumes: 10% @ 100M, 18% @ 500M, 28% @ 1B (custom pricing and SLAs available for larger commitments).

Next steps:
1) If that looks in-range, Marissa (cc'd) can pull together a short mutual action plan and a draft volume discount schedule.
2) If you want p50/p95 latencies and instance sizing guidance for demo spikes, Ben can run a quick simulation with your expected request/sequence length profile.
3) We can set up a 30-min call this week to walk the doc and answer procurement questions.

Quick Q: can you share a rough average sequence length (tokens in + tokens out) for the 10M/month estimate? That helps us recommend model tiers and batching settings.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
redwood.com

Thanks Logan — that helps a lot.

A couple quick follow-ups:
1) For our initial 10M tokens/month estimate, average sequence length is roughly 120 tokens (40 in / 80 out). We expect demo spikes where short bursts hit ~1.5x baseline for a few hours.
2) Do the discounts you listed apply retroactively for monthly overage, or only to committed pool usage?
3) Any evaluation/demo discount or trial credits available for first 30 days so we can instrument quality metrics without committing up front?

If you can point me to the short PDF (can't open drive at the moment), feel free to paste the main table inline — otherwise we'll download later. Would be great to schedule a 30-min call with Marissa next week; she can coordinate internally on procurement.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Cory
